title: VPC deployment certification: gateway health & model instantiation validation
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Purpose: provide an automated, repeatable certification pipeline that validates a freshly provisioned VPC/private deployment meets runtime readiness criteria before marking a customer rollout as healthy. Scope includes: validating control-plane gateway connectivity, API request/response correctness, model artifact unpack + sanity generation, KV cache bootstrap, and Terraform output/invariant checks that ensure idempotent upgrades. This ticket implements the orchestration and wiring for the verification stage in the IaC pipeline (Terraform -> CI -> certification).
acceptance_criteria: A1: CI job runs after Terraform apply and returns PASS/FAIL with structured artifacts (logs, traces, metrics) stored in the deployment bucket.
A2: Gateway-level tests validate TLS, client-cert, and header-based routing within 10s on an empty cluster.
A3: API readiness check returns stable 2xx responses for standard endpoints (/v1/health, /v1/models, /v1/generate) for 3 consecutive samples at 5s intervals.

A4: Model instantiation test loads the pinned model variant, runs a 64-token generation with a deterministic prompt, and validates output token count and kv-cache warmup metrics are within expected thresholds.

A5: Upgrade-safety check confirms that terraform plan/apply has preserved critical invariants (security groups, private subnets, KMS key rotation policy) and flags any destructive changes for manual review.
A6: Failure modes produce actionable errors and link to runbook sections for remediation.
A7: Tests run in under 15 minutes for a standard dedicated node pool size (4x A100-configured nodes) or provide a clear reason for longer runs.
A8: Artifacts include links to the failing step log, associated GitHub PR, Confluence remediation doc, and the customer deployment id.
A9: The job returns an exit code consumed by rollout automation to decide canary progression or rollback.
A10: Audit events are emitted to the central audit log for each certification attempt (success/failure) with correlation IDs.
test_plan: 1) Terraform apply -> CI trigger: use existing terraform pipeline; append a certification stage that invokes the cert-orchestrator container.
2) Gateway health: curl --http2 --resolve to gateway DNS, validate TLS chain and 200 from /v1/health; retry 3x with 5s fbackoff.
3) API smoke: call /v1/models and assert expected model names from provisioned manifest; call /v1/generate with deterministic prompt and verify non-empty output and 200 status.
4) Model load test: request a single warm-start allocation, then a 64-token generation measuring first-token latency, median token time, and kv-cache hit ratio logged to metrics endpoint.
5) Concurrency sweep: exercise 1, 5, 20 concurrent small requests to ensure router/backpressure behaves and no request queue growth beyond threshold.

6) Idempotency/upgrade check: run terraform plan twice; verify no drift; then run a benign module upgrade (version bump) and ensure certification still passes or produces documented non-blocking warnings.
7) Negative tests: simulate model artifact checksum mismatch and confirm job surfaces 'model artifact mismatch' with remediation steps and aborts rollout.
8) Clean-up sanity: ensure objects created for test (temp buckets, jobs) are deleted and secrets rotated if test keys were used.
9) Timeouts & circuit breakers: validate the orchestrator respects global test timeout of 15m and returns structured failure state on timeout.
10) Metrics & dashboards: certify that the job emits metrics (cert.duration, cert.failures, cert.step.latency) to Datadog with tags: env, deployment_id, terraform_workspace.
11) Compliance: if KMS keys are present, run an encryption-check step that verifies CMK policy and logs to audit trail.
12) Canary gating: integrate with rollout controller so that a failed certification blocks canary >1 and prints failure summary in rollout UI.
13) Manual override: document how to force-accept a deployment (rare) and require a JIRA/approval link in the override reason.
14) Recovery: include a remediation path to re-run certification on the same deployment after fixes without reapplying infra when safe.
15) Resource quotas: ensure test stage respects cost limits and optionally uses smaller model variant for cheaper smoke runs when flagged.
runbook: Runbook overview: cert-orchestrator job lives in ci/certification/pipelines and runs post-apply. It has steps: infra-check -> gateway-check -> api-smoke -> model-load -> kv-bootstrap -> metrics-check -> finalize.
Step: infra-check: validate terraform outputs (vpc_id, private_subnet_ids, bastion_ip, cert_dns). If outputs missing, mark failure with 'terraform-output-missing'.

Step: gateway-check: verify ALB/NLB health, listener configuration and target group readiness. Common failures: wrong security group, listener using wrong cert. Fix: compare terraform cert_arn with ACM and reconcile.
Step: api-smoke: run scripted HTTP checks with authentication token rotation. If 401 returned, confirm OIDC client secret in secrets manager matches terraform output.
Step: model-load: run the instantiate command against nodes and capture logs. If model binary fails checksum, surface S3 path, expected checksum, and actual checksum.
Step: kv-bootstrap: send a curated prompt set to prime KV and assert kv-cache-hit metric > 0. If not, look at redis connection config and pod affinity.
Step: finalize: emit cert.result metric and write a certification.json artifact to the deployment bucket with summary and step-level logs.

Remediation patterns: security-group mismatch -> re-apply with corrected sg; model checksum -> re-upload artifact with correct checksum and restart model-puller; API auth fail -> rotate client secret and re-run job.
Contact: on-call infra (pager duty: infra-oncall) and runtime lead (Devon Clarke) for escalations.
Manual rerun: ci pipeline supports toggling --replay to skip terraform apply and re-run checks when infra unchanged.
Audit: every run stores a run_manifest with correlation_id which must be attached to any postmortem for failures.
Security note: tests should never log plaintext secrets. Masking enforced by the orchestrator; if leak detected, notify security and rotate affected secrets.
Permissions: certification job runs with a least-privilege role; make sure it has read access to deployment bucket and kms:Decrypt for test keys.
SLAs: certification job should not extend rollout by more than 30m in normal cases; long-running certs should be flagged 'investigate'.

notes: Implementation must avoid storing any production customer PII in test artifacts. Use masked deployment ids and rotate any test credentials immediately after runs. Prefer model-lite smoke variants for cost-sensitive work but always run full model-load as gating step for dedicated deployments.
dev_todo: Finish PR review for infra/pull/1845, add terraform output extractor script to infra repo, wire CI trigger in ENG-30142 pipeline, coordinate threshold numbers with benchmarking team.
observability_requirements: Emit metrics: cert.duration, cert.step.failure{step}, cert.kvcache.hit_ratio, cert.model.first_token_latency. Include tags: deployment_id, workspace, terraform_version, cert_attempt_id. Logs: structured JSON per-step with correlation_id.
postmortem_policy: If certification fails for more than 3 consecutive customer deployments in a single week, create a blameless postmortem and tag runtime and infra leads. Attach certification artifacts in the postmortem.
customer_notes: For Managed customers: certification is run before canary promotion. If a certification failure blocks rollout, customer will receive an automated digest with failure summary and ETA for re-run after remediation.
implementation_decisions: 1) Use a containerized cert-orchestrator in CI to isolate runtime dependencies. 2) Use existing Datadog for metrics and S3 for artifacts instead of introducing a new storage service. 3) Default to doing cheap smoke on small model variant but gate final pass on the provisioned model for Dedicated deployments.
security_notes: KMS checks and audit log writes are mandatory. Certification job should assume no privilege to change infra. Any step that would modify Terraform-managed resources must return a warning and require manual intervention.
community_impact: This suite will reduce post-deploy incidents by catching model-instantiation regressions early. Expect initial flakiness during rollout; plan to run two warm-up cycles in staging before enabling for production customers.
